clue.text: Top level achieved by worthy, which is evident when paper comes to light?

blocks.note: high in the sense of morally lofty, high-minded

blocks.clueFragment: which is evident when paper comes to light
blocks.note: a faint design pressed into paper that shows when it is held up to the light

explanation.surface: Someone worthy reaches the peak of their career, and the news is revealed once the paper comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes to light' sounds like news breaking, but it means paper literally held up to light, where its watermark shows.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point reached by a flood tide is the literal sense; figuratively it is any peak of achievement.

clue.text: Shoddy plane ascending with sign of metal fatigue?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

explanation.surface: A badly made aircraft climbing away with a fracture showing in its fuselage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcrack describes cheap, flimsy, showy goods, which matches poorly made or shoddy work.

clue.text: Endless rush - don't hang around!

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: to shoot is to dash or rush along

explanation.surface: An urgent command to someone to hurry off and not linger.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is the exclamation used to drive away a person or animal, telling them to go away at once.

clue.text: Fine female on colt crossing our meadow and meeting sweetheart - a lucky discovery?

indicators.note: the outer letters cross over and so enclose what is named after this word
coming together signals that the next part is simply joined on at the end

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
C is the racing abbreviation for colt
lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: A girl riding a young horse across our field meets her beau, which seems a stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so female sits on top of colt; the meadow then goes inside, just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding a rare clover plant with four leaves instead of three is traditionally a sign of good luck.

clue.text: Supposed river would join sea

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A geographical assumption that a river would flow into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Deemed means judged or considered, which is to say thought or supposed to be so.

clue.text: Future bride on bike - companion with a trendy floral decoration

blocks.note: Daisy is the girl in the song 'Daisy Bell', proposed to on a bicycle built for two

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be cycling with her friend while wearing a fashionable garland of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The old music-hall song 'Daisy Bell' asks Daisy for her answer, on the seat of a bicycle made for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Children thread small white flowers together stem to stem to make a garland worn as decoration.

clue.text: Ordinary concern for money made from investment?

blocks.note: a concern is something you have an interest in

explanation.surface: An everyday worry about returns on one's savings.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings calculated only on the original principal, not compounded, are a basic return on capital lent or deposited.

clue.text: Leader's policy, which dominates the front page

blocks.note: a head is a leader; the possessive joins the next piece
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A political leader's stance is splashed across the top of the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The large-type title on a newspaper's first sheet is what catches the eye and dominates it.

clue.text: Language from woman's hard to follow

indicators.note: one piece coming after another means it is placed at the end

blocks.note: a woman's name; the 's reads as 'has'
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A woman's language is difficult to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish Gaelic is the Celtic tongue spoken in Ireland, one of the country's official languages.

clue.text: Choose time for entering - I have key

indicators.note: going in means one word is placed inside the other

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Picking a moment to get in, because I hold the key to the door.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'the operative word', it means the significant or crucial one, so key in the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Match-goer dissolving in the mass

indicators.note: something dissolving breaks up and loses its shape, so the letters fall apart and reform

explanation.surface: A football fan melting into the crowd at the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The mass' looks like a crowd of people, but mass is the physical quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectogram is a metric unit of weight equal to one hundred grams, so a measure of mass.

clue.text: Unhappy about baked dish - not entirely tasty

indicators.note: not the whole thing means the last letter is cut off
around means the first word wraps the second

explanation.surface: Someone disappointed by a baked dish that isn't wholly flavoursome.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid is a formal word meaning having a strong, pleasant flavour, so savoury or tasty.

clue.text: Quarrel in which wife has right perspective

blocks.note: an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: A domestic row where the wife has the correct point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrangle is to argue noisily or at length, which is a synonym for quarrelling.

clue.text: See 1
A sort of biologist, I get insect dissected

indicators.note: a dissected specimen is cut apart, so these letters are taken to pieces and reassembled

explanation.surface: A biologist describing their work of cutting up insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies heredity and genes is a specialist within the broad field of biology.

clue.text: Detective being a man of many words

blocks.note: dick is old slang for a private detective
ens is the philosophical term for an entity or being

explanation.surface: A detective who talks a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens wrote long novels, often published in serial instalments, so he produced a great volume of prose.

clue.text: Screen is put up on day before festival

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: an eve is the day before a feast such as Christmas

explanation.surface: A film shown on the evening before a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' looks like showing a film, but here it is a noun for a mesh that filters.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen in the sense of a mesh for separating fine material from coarse is a riddle or strainer.

clue.text: Given a fair treat or treated unfairly?

blocks.note: first meaning: literally given a go on a fairground attraction
second meaning: the idiom for being cheated or deceived

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' in the first half is a funfair, set against 'unfairly' in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means being given a trip on something, and idiomatically means being swindled or duped.

clue.text: See 17
Reactionary types - are they getting hot under the collar?

definitions.text: are they getting hot under the collar?

blocks.clueFragment: are they getting hot under the collar?
blocks.note: second meaning: angry people flush, so the skin above the collar turns colour

explanation.walkthrough: The question reads the word literally: people getting hot under the collar might well have flushed necks.
explanation.definitionFit: The American slang term for poor, white, rural conservatives with prejudiced views fits right-wing reactionaries.

clue.text: See 17
See 7
Embrocation with no name working like a machine

indicators.note: lacking means the letters of the next word are taken out of the first
something being worked is kneaded into a new form, so the remaining letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, and its letters are removed

explanation.surface: A liniment with no brand name that works mechanically.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking N, A, M and E out of embrocation leaves B, R, O, C, T, I, O to rearrange. Embrocation is a rubbing liniment.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic describes movement or behaviour that is mechanical and stiff, as a machine's would be.

clue.text: Great little woman's participation in more than one match

definitions.text: participation in more than one match

blocks.note: Amy March is one of the four sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A small woman who has played a fine part in several sporting fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a game; here it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy is the crime of going through a marriage ceremony while already legally married to someone else.

clue.text: See 4
Grubby little area?

blocks.note: surface reading: a small dirty patch or corner
setter's reading: to do with grub, slang for food, so a small space for eating meals

explanation.walkthrough: Grubby normally means dirty, but grub is slang for food, so the clue means a small spot where food is eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an alcove or small room set aside for eating, often just off a kitchen.

clue.text: Smartness of soldier in coat

indicators.note: one thing being inside another means it is placed within it

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier looking smart in his coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic can mean a wonderful skill or cleverness, as in a player's magic, close to smartness or brilliance.

clue.text: See 1
Chaps at the very top ruling cricket?

definitions.text: Chaps at the very top ruling

blocks.note: an over is a set of six balls, and Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London

explanation.surface: The men who run the game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the wordplay as an example: two cricket words, OVER and LORDS, joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are supreme rulers holding power over others, so men in the highest positions of command.

clue.text: See 8
Water below doesn't move audibly

indicators.note: heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: Still water beneath us that makes no noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below' means the underworld, not simply lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Styx is the river of the underworld, so it is water in the realm below.

clue.text: Meat and drink - first and last items of picnics by tree

indicators.note: only the opening and closing letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: the opening and closing letters of the word

explanation.surface: Picnic supplies of food and drink laid out beside a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump steak is a cut of beef taken from the hindquarters, so a kind of meat.

clue.text: A street in American city can be frightful

indicators.note: being within means these words are placed inside the city

explanation.surface: A road in a US city that can be a scary place.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means very unpleasant or horrible, which is what frightful means in everyday use.
